mechanism_narrative: The strong and consistent upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity, which will continue to drive retail and recreation visits higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days, despite the observed upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The significant increase in WORKPLACES mobility, reaching above -45% baseline at t-0w, signals a critical mass of people returning to offices, which will directly translate to increased retail and recreation activity during workdays over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility is above -45% baseline at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, despite WORKPLACES mobility remaining above -45% baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a sustained shift in behavior where people are spending less time at home, directly freeing up time and opportunity for out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days decreases or remains flat, while RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The significant and accelerating increase in TRANSIT station visits suggests a broader return to public transportation for commuting and leisure, which will facilitate greater access to and participation in retail and recreation activities over the next four weeks, assuming no new restrictions.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, despite TRANSIT mobility continuing its upward trend and no new restrictions being implemented.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp and accelerating recovery in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, reaching near-baseline levels, indicates a general increase in comfort with out-of-home activities and a return to routine errands, which will spill over into increased RETAIL_REC within the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days decreases or remains flat, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility remaining strong or increasing further.

mechanism_narrative: The combined trend of decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility and increasing WORKPLACES mobility signifies a fundamental shift from home-centric to out-of-home activities, particularly work-related commuting, which creates more opportunities for retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, despite WORKPLACES mobility increasing and RESIDENTIAL mobility decreasing.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent increase in PARKS mobility, especially the recent acceleration, indicates growing public comfort with outdoor leisure and public spaces. This increased comfort will extend to other out-of-home activities, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks, provided PARKS mobility remains above -50% baseline.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility is above -50% baseline at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days decreases or remains flat, despite PARKS mobility remaining above -50% baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based and accelerating recovery across all mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES) and the decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility strongly imply an underlying policy shift towards significant reopening, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC upwards over the next four weeks, assuming no policy reversal.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, or if any major policy reversal (e.g., new lockdown measures) is announced.
